traceability.evidence:
1) Tests explicitly tied to this story all pass (from `npm test -- --verbose`): - tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts – "Maintenance CLI (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)": covers - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect exits 0 with no stale annotations; detect supports --json and returns code 1 with a JSON payload when stale annotations exist; detect with non-existent --root exits 0 and reports no stale annotations. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verify exits 0 when annotations are valid. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] report prints a human-readable summary (Markdown-style header plus stale path) and exits 0. - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] update rewrites @story old.path.md → new.path.md and exits 0. - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] update without --from/--to exits 2 and logs error + help; dry-run does not change files and exits 0; invalid --format value exits 2 with a precise error; permission errors during detect are caught and reported as "traceability-maint failed: ..." with exit code 2; no subcommand prints help and exits 0. - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts – "detectStaleAnnotations isolated (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)": - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] returns [] when directory does not exist; detects stale annotations in nested directories; ensures security behavior by verifying fs.existsSync is never called for unsafe/traversal/invalid-extension story paths but is called for normalized in-workspace paths. - tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts – verifies detectStaleAnnotations returns [] when no stale annotations and returns a single stale story path when present. - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts – "updateAnnotationReferences isolated": - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] updates @story old.path.md → new.path.md in-place and returns count 1; returns 0 when directory does not exist. - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts – confirms updateAnnotationReferences returns 0 when no updates are needed. - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts – "batchUpdateAnnotations / verifyAnnotations": - [REQ-MAINT-BATCH] returns 0 when mappings array is empty. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] returns true when @story has a corresponding .story.md file. - tests/maintenance/report.test.ts – "generateMaintenanceReport": - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] returns empty string when no stale annotations; includes stale story path when present. - tests/maintenance/index.test.ts – confirms all maintenance exports exist: - detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport.
2) Implementation of maintenance helpers (programmatic API) under src/maintenance: - src/maintenance/index.ts: - Exports detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport. - Annotated with @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and all REQ-MAINT-* IDs. - src/maintenance/detect.ts: - function detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] implements REQ-MAINT-DETECT and REQ-MAINT-SAFE by: - Resolving a workspaceRoot from process.cwd() and codebasePath; returning [] if it does not exist or is not a directory. - Walking all files via getAllFiles(workspaceRoot). - Parsing @story annotations, using isUnsafeStoryPath and enforceProjectBoundary to ignore unsafe/out-of-project paths. - Checking existence only for in-project candidates and adding storyPath to a Set when none exist on disk. - Catching file read and boundary errors so detection continues safely. - src/maintenance/update.ts: - function updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath, oldPath, newPath): number implements REQ-MAINT-UPDATE by: - Returning 0 if codebasePath is not an existing directory (safe noop). - Using a regex `(@story\s*)` and a helper processFileForAnnotationUpdates to: - Skip non-file entries. - Replace only the @story path fragment, increment a replacement counter, and write back only when content changed (preserving other code and formatting). - src/maintenance/batch.ts: - function batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath, mappings): number implements REQ-MAINT-BATCH by iterating mappings and summing updateAnnotationReferences results. - function verifyAnnotations(codebasePath): boolean implements REQ-MAINT-VERIFY by returning detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath).length === 0. - src/maintenance/report.ts: - function generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath): string implements REQ-MAINT-REPORT and REQ-MAINT-SAFE by returning "" when no stale annotations, otherwise a newline-separated list of stale @story paths. - src/maintenance/utils.ts: - getAllFiles(dir: string): string[] encapsulates recursive traversal and directory validation for the maintenance tools, supporting safe, consistent file walking.
3) CLI implementation and UX for maintenance tools: - package.json: - "bin": { "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js" } – provides the maintenance CLI as required by the story. - src/maintenance/cli.ts: - Exports runMaintenanceCli(rawArgv: string[]): number; uses normalizeCliArgs and dispatches to subcommand handlers. - Provides help when no subcommand or -h/--help is passed; prints comprehensive usage text describing commands and options. - Wraps dispatch in a try/catch; on error logs "traceability-maint failed: " to stderr and returns EXIT_USAGE (2), satisfying REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - src/maintenance/commands.ts: - Defines exit codes: EXIT_OK=0, EXIT_STALE=1, EXIT_USAGE=2, aligned with docs. - handleDetect: parses flags, calls detectStaleAnnotations, prints human-readable summary or JSON `{ root, stale }`, and returns proper exit codes (0/1). - handleVerify: uses verifyAnnotations, prints success or guidance text, returns 0/1. - handleReport: uses generateMaintenanceReport, supports `--format text|json`, prints either Markdown-style human-readable report or JSON `{ root, report }`, always returns 0. - handleUpdate: validates required --from/--to, supports --dry-run and --json, uses updateAnnotationReferences for real updates, and returns correct exit codes (0 or 2 on usage error), honoring REQ-MAINT-UPDATE and REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - src/maintenance/flags.ts: - parseCliInput, normalizeCliArgs, parseFlags implement minimal, predictable argument/flag parsing with validation of --format values and defaults for root/json/dry-run.
4) Documentation for maintenance tools (fulfilling Documentation & UX criteria): - README.md – "Maintenance CLI" section: - Explains purpose of `traceability-maint` (maintain and audit @story annotations, focus on stale references and safe batch updates). - Lists commands (detect, verify, report, update) with one-line descriptions. - Provides concrete usage examples for each command. - Links to user-docs/api-reference.md#maintenance-api-and-cli for full details. - user-docs/api-reference.md – "Maintenance API and CLI" section: - Describes programmatic maintenance API functions (detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport) including parameters, return types, and behavior notes that match the implementation. - Fully documents CLI usage, options, JSON payload shapes, and exit codes for detect/verify/report/update, aligned with src/maintenance/commands.ts. - docs/decisions/adr-maintenance-cli-interface.md: - ADR explicitly references docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and documents the chosen CLI design, commands, exit codes, and testing approach; actual code and tests conform to this ADR.
Overall, all REQ-MAINT-* requirements have direct implementations and passing tests, and there is clear user-facing documentation for both the API and CLI.
traceability.notes: Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS requires helper tools to detect, update, batch-update, verify, and report on traceability annotations, with safe behavior, CLI integration, and documentation. The project provides a complete maintenance API under src/maintenance, a published CLI binary traceability-maint with subcommands detect/verify/report/update, and comprehensive Jest tests that are explicitly linked to this story and exercise all REQ-MAINT-* requirements and edge cases. README.md and user-docs/api-reference.md document the maintenance API and CLI usage, options, and exit codes. All relevant tests pass, and the behavior observed in code, tests, and docs aligns with the acceptance criteria, so this story is fully implemented.
